verdict_text:
YES

The script drops every tensor whose block index is in {2, 6, 10, 14}, renumbers survivors by enumerating the kept indices in ascending order (yielding exactly the mapping in clause 2), passes the 4 non-block tensors through untouched, and writes a single `out/T1/model.safetensors`. The renumbering is done into a fresh dict, so no collision is possible. The asserts run before `save_file`, so a failure produces a non-zero exit with no output written; the set-equality assert on surviving layer indices implies both "no block 12..15 remains" and "exactly 12 blocks", and the length assert enforces 184 tensors.

One note outside the specification text: the script imports `load_checkpoint` from a sibling `_ckpt` module, which makes it not strictly self-contained, but the task specification itself does not prohibit that.
